mentions.name: Flakiness.io
mentions.description: This service provides test analytics for GitHub and GitLab, connecting test results and artifacts with commit history and testing environment so test reports can show whether a pull request failure is a real regression or a known flake from the target branch. Its core is a specialized analytics engine for storing and querying large amounts of test results, with 2.5 billion test results processed to date. It offers a 1GB free plan (roughly 10M+ test results), with limits increasable to 100GB for large open source projects.
mentions.problem: It is hard to tell whether a pull request test failure is a real regression or a known flake from the target branch.
mentions.audience: Developers and QA engineers using GitHub or GitLab CI, including large open source projects (e.g., nuxt/nuxt, wordpress/gutenberg).
mentions.source_excerpt:
https://flakiness.io: test analytics for GitHub and GitLab.

The idea is to connect test results and artifacts with commit history and testing environment. This way test reports can show whether a failure in a pull request is a real regression or a known flake from a target branch.

The core of the service is a specialized analytics engine that makes it possible to store and query large amounts of test results [1]. Thanks to this engine, we've processed 2.5 billion test results to date.
